construction: 598 parts in 81 steps across 20 sections: the `Prop Plane` root (fuselage of 1×16 and 1×12 Technic bricks and plates), `Engine block`, `Piston`, `Piston gear`, `Bottom gear` ×2, `Bottom link`, `Bottom back connector`, `Pontoons` with three joint children, `Triangle joint`, `Tail` with `Tail body`, `Wings` with two joints and two flaps, and the `Pilot`.
interfaces: 327 studs up, 62 sideways, 198 angled. The wing's universal joints and towballs sit on the fuselage cabane; the floats' truss apexes pin under the fuselage; the propeller axle drives the piston through gears.
lesson: The 1988 studded Technic floatplane: a Technic-brick fuselage with an open cockpit and pilot, a high wing of Technic-brick spars and wing-brick ribs on universal joints, a piston engine behind a three-blade propeller, a tail boom with a 7×12 wing-plate tailplane and jumper-plate fin, and twin floats on an axle truss with wheels inside. Measured: span 72 studs, length 50, height 26, 598 parts, 66% Technic.
parent_context: Root section; nothing places it. Built with the propeller at +Z, so LeoCAD's front view is the tail-on view.
reuse_notes: Use it for the proportions and module layout of a studded Technic floatplane: span 1.4× length, high wing, floats two-thirds of the length. Inspiration only: the author scaled or skewed eight placements to match the strained real model, so rebuild rather than export.
